doc.title: Ralph Humphrey interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: John Klemmer
summary: Humphrey met Klemmer in Don Ellis's band and describes him as an early New Age saxophonist who disappeared from public view.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah. You played with John Klemmer?
Played with John Klemmer. He was actually in Don’s band, that’s where I met him.
Whatever happened to John Klemmer, do you know?

Well I see that John was maybe one of the first New Age saxophone players, you know, with what he was doing back, way back when. A phenomenal player. Really a wonderful jazz player. But I think John had some, maybe some psychological problems and so it kind of made him disappear from the public for a while. And I really haven’t followed his career so I don’t know what he’s doing. I think he’s still recording though.
